description: Crystal defects decomposed. Vacancies (Schottky, Frenkel), interstitials, substitutional solutes, edge + screw dislocations, Burgers vectors, dislocation interactions, twin boundaries, stacking faults, dislocation density evolution.

sub_mechanisms.name: Schottky_defect
sub_mechanisms.definition: Vacancy + missing counter-ion in ionic crystal. Maintains charge neutrality.
sub_mechanisms.why: Standard in ionic crystals. Concentration ∝ exp(-E/2kT). Conductivity mechanism in solid electrolytes.

sub_mechanisms.name: Frenkel_defect
sub_mechanisms.definition: Ion displaced from lattice site to interstitial position. Vacancy + interstitial pair.
sub_mechanisms.why: Smaller ions (e.g., Ag⁺) common. Used to explain ionic conduction in AgCl. Standard.

sub_mechanisms.name: edge_dislocation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Extra half-plane of atoms inserted in lattice. Edge of half-plane = dislocation line.
sub_mechanisms.why: Easy slip mechanism. Burgers vector perpendicular to line. Foundation of plasticity.

sub_mechanisms.name: screw_dislocation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Helical distortion. Burgers vector parallel to dislocation line.
sub_mechanisms.why: Crystal growth (spiral growth). Cross-slip possible (changes slip plane).

sub_mechanisms.name: Burgers_vector
sub_mechanisms.definition: Vector closure failure around dislocation. Magnitude + direction.
sub_mechanisms.why: Slip direction + magnitude. Foundation of dislocation theory. Determines slip systems.

sub_mechanisms.name: Peierls_stress
sub_mechanisms.definition: Stress required to move dislocation in perfect lattice. Lower than yield.
sub_mechanisms.why: Intrinsic resistance to slip. Higher in BCC (ductile-brittle transition). Foundation.

sub_mechanisms.name: dislocation_interaction
sub_mechanisms.definition: Dislocations attract/repel. Cutting + jogs. Pinning at obstacles.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of work hardening. Dislocation density increases → mutual obstacles → higher stress required. Tangled forests.

sub_mechanisms.name: slip_systems
sub_mechanisms.definition: Plane + direction along which dislocations move. FCC: 12 systems {111}<110>.
sub_mechanisms.why: Determines plastic deformation. FCC active at all T (12 systems); BCC inactive at low T. Foundation of ductility.

sub_mechanisms.name: twin_boundary
sub_mechanisms.definition: Mirror plane in crystal. One side mirror image of other.
sub_mechanisms.why: Deformation twinning at low T (hcp, bcc). Annealing twins in FCC. Standard microstructural feature.

sub_mechanisms.name: stacking_fault
sub_mechanisms.definition: Error in stacking sequence (ABCABC interrupted). Energy per area.
sub_mechanisms.why: Low SFE: easy dislocation dissociation, twinning common. Cu low, Al high. Influences strengthening.

sub_mechanisms.name: Frank_Read_source
sub_mechanisms.definition: Dislocation segment between pinning points; bows under stress; multiplies.
sub_mechanisms.why: Dislocation multiplication mechanism. Explains how density grows during deformation. Foundation.

sub_mechanisms.name: grain_boundary_strengthening
sub_mechanisms.definition: GBs pin dislocations. Hall-Petch: σ_y = σ_0 + k·d^(-1/2).
sub_mechanisms.why: Smaller grains = more boundaries = stronger. Universal strengthening mechanism. Already in main; here mechanism.

derivation_rules.name: dislocation_glide_easier_than_lattice_shear
then: dislocation glide is the mechanism, not rigid shear
derivation_rules.why: Rigid shear: all bonds simultaneously, GPa stress. Dislocation: one bond at a time, MPa. Foundation of plasticity (Orowan + Taylor 1934).

derivation_rules.name: FCC_ductile_at_all_T
then: ductile from cryogenic to high T
derivation_rules.why: 12 active slip systems at any T. BCC: 12 but Peierls stress high at low T → brittle. HCP: limited systems. Foundation of cryogenic materials.

derivation_rules.name: Frank_Read_explains_density_increase
derivation_rules.why: Initial: ~10⁶ /cm². Heavily worked: 10¹². Need source. Frank-Read: bowing dislocation multiplies. Foundation work hardening.

derivation_rules.name: low_SFE_enables_twinning
derivation_rules.why: Low SFE: dissociated dislocations don't recombine to cross-slip. Twinning easier. TWIP steels exploit (twinning-induced plasticity).

derivation_rules.name: grain_boundary_pinning_strengthens
derivation_rules.why: GB acts as obstacle. Pile-up creates stress concentration → activates adjacent grain. Hall-Petch quantifies. Foundation strengthening.
